answer: Grading uses linkable ring signatures: a grader signs inside a ferrous ring of peers, so nobody - author or vote partner - can tell who scored, breaking reciprocal 'you rate me, I rate you' deals. Each carries a copper linkability tag, so double-grading or one key across several wallets resolves to the same tag. A verdict later found corrupt opens the ring and slashes the real signer; honest graders stay anonymous. A reef of cloned ballots shares one tag and collapses into a slashable cluster. Cost: one genuine judgment and key per identity; collusion is traced, not hidden.
